comments.body:
═══ DESIGN DIRECTION FROM THE OPERATOR: move the shared ticket details into the SYSTEM PROMPT so the
common input is cacheable across the batch. ═══

Recording this as the chosen approach, plus the one measurement that decides whether it pays off.

**THE DESIGN.** Today `judge_one` puts BOTH digests in the volatile instructions:

    system_prompt = <constant ~459 tokens>
    instructions  = f"FIRST:\n{_digest_block(first)}\n\nSECOND:\n{_digest_block(second)}"

`first` (the query ticket's digest) is IDENTICAL across every call in a batch — only `second` varies.
Moving `first` into the system prompt makes the cacheable prefix `system + FIRST`, written once and
read on the remaining N-1 calls. This is the same byte-stable-prefix / volatile-body split the engine
already uses at `workflow/runs.py:245` via `prompts.resolve_prompt_cached` and the `<!--volatile-->`
marker (story c6e5), so it follows an established in-repo pattern rather than inventing one.

**THE CACHE IS WARM WITHIN A BATCH, NOT ACROSS REVIEWS** — worth stating so nobody expects more. The
prefix is stable for the 18 calls of ONE review (same query ticket) and changes on the next review of
a different ticket. So the win is 1 write + 17 reads per review, comfortably inside the cache TTL. A
repeat review of the SAME ticket inside the TTL would also hit, but that is a bonus, not the case to
design for.

**THE ONE THING THAT DECIDES WHETHER THIS PAYS OFF — and it must be measured, not assumed.**

    measured system prompt:        ~459 tokens
    measured mean per-call input:  2,086 tokens
    => instructions (FIRST + SECOND + scaffolding) ≈ 1,627, so each digest ≈ 800
    => the proposed prefix (system + FIRST) ≈ 1,250 tokens   <-- ESTIMATE, must be measured directly

`CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS = 4096` would make a ~1,250-token prefix uncacheable, and the change would
write and read nothing.

**BUT THAT FLOOR IS MODEL-DEPENDENT, AND ITS OWN COMMENT SAYS SO** — `pass1.py` documents 4096 as
"the minimum prompt-prefix the anthropic cache will write/read (**Opus 4.8 floor**)". Anthropic's
minimum cacheable prefix differs by model. Since `afeb` moves `overlap-judge` off the frontier default
onto `standard` (or `trivial`), **the floor that actually applies after `afeb` may not be 4096.** That
interaction is the crux of this ticket and must be established first, in whichever direction it falls:

- if the applicable floor is BELOW the measured prefix → this design works, implement it and prove it
  with `cache_read_tokens > 0` on a repeat run;
- if the applicable floor is ABOVE it → moving FIRST into the system prompt is necessary but NOT
  sufficient, and the ticket must fall back to reducing call volume (batching N candidates per call,
  or tightening BM25F retrieval) which raises the prefix past the floor as a side effect.

So the first work item is: measure the real `system + FIRST` token count, and determine the true
minimum cacheable prefix for the model class `afeb` assigns — not the Opus constant, unless Opus is
what ends up running it.

**SEQUENCING, restated:** `afeb` lands first. It sets both the model class AND therefore the floor
that applies, so measuring before it lands would measure the wrong baseline twice over.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
═══ OPERATOR REQUIREMENT: warm the cache BEFORE fanning out parallel judge calls. Recorded, with the
measurement that says when it binds — and why ignoring it would make parallelism a REGRESSION. ═══

**MEASURED: the judge loop is SEQUENTIAL today.** From the same instrumented run:

    18 overlap-judge calls, span 25.1s, mean gap 1.48s, min gap 1.23s

and the code agrees — `overlap/judge.py:judge` (:117) is a plain `for cand in candidates:` (:131)
with no thread pool or async. So cold-start is currently handled by accident of ordering: the first
call writes the cache and the remaining 17 read it. **No warm-up is needed while it stays sequential.**

**WHY THE REQUIREMENT MATTERS THE MOMENT IT IS PARALLELIZED — and parallelizing is tempting, because
25.1s of wall-clock per plan review for ADVISORY output is a real latency cost.** Fan out N cold calls
that share a cacheable prefix and every one of them MISSES and every one of them WRITES. On Anthropic
a cache write costs MORE than ordinary input (a premium over base input price), while a read costs a
small fraction of it. So the naive parallel version pays ~18 premium writes instead of 1 write + 17
cheap reads — **strictly worse than the sequential version it replaced, and worse than no caching at
all.** An "optimization" that increases cost is the failure mode to design against here.

**THE SHAPE THE OPERATOR SPECIFIED, and it gets both wins:** issue ONE call first and let it complete
(writing the shared prefix into the cache), THEN fan out the remaining N-1 in parallel, all reading.
Result: 1 write + 17 reads for cost, and wall-clock of roughly one call plus one parallel batch instead
of 18 serial calls. The two goals — cheap via cache, fast via parallelism — only compose in that order.

**A GOTCHA IF THREADS ARE USED, which connects to story b690.** `workflow/map_fanout.py` is the
in-repo precedent for concurrency (`ThreadPoolExecutor`), and a ContextVar is inherited by asyncio
tasks but **NOT by raw threads**. Story b690 added per-step usage-log attribution
(`usage_log.step_identity` -> the `step` / `model_class` columns) via a ContextVar. `map_fanout` stays
correct only because the binding happens INSIDE each worker (`_map_iteration` -> `_run_leaf` binds in
the worker's own thread). **If overlap judging is parallelized with a thread pool and the binding is
left outside the pool, every judge call silently loses its `step`/`model_class` attribution** — the
exact observability this epic just built, and the thing that made this ticket's measurements possible.
Bind inside the worker, and assert it in a test.

**ADDITIONAL ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA**
- [ ] if the judge loop is parallelized, the shared prefix is warmed by a COMPLETED first call before
      any fan-out begins; asserted by a test, not by ordering that happens to work
- [ ] the before/after comparison reports `cache_write_tokens` as well as `cache_read_tokens` and
      input tokens — a design that turns 1 write into N writes must show up as a FAILURE, and reads
      alone would hide it
- [ ] if a thread pool is used, per-call `step`/`model_class` attribution survives (bind the
      ContextVar inside the worker); asserted by reading a usage log produced by a parallel run
- [ ] the advisory fail-safe still holds under concurrency: one judge call failing must not fail the
      review, and must not corrupt the others' results

comments.body:
═══ MEASURED, POST-`afeb`, AGAINST THE REAL API. The floor is 1024, not 4096 — and the prefix
today lands just under it. ═══

Three measurements, all from real `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6` calls, not from reading code.

**1. THE PREFIX IS GENUINELY RE-SENT PER CALL (observed, not inferred).** A recording proxy runner
wrapped the real runner around `overlap.judge.judge()` over a 6-candidate corpus of REAL digests
(produced by `rebar.llm.enrich` on 7 live tickets). 12 calls (6 candidates x 2 orderings):

    distinct system prompts                                   1  (byte-identical, 377 tokens)
    calls whose USER message contains the query digest block  12 / 12   <- re-sent every time
    query digest block                                        308 tokens
    mean instructions (FIRST + SECOND + scaffolding)          608 tokens
    total input                                        16,040 tokens   (per call 1,273-1,420)
    cache_read_tokens                                         0
    cache_write_tokens                                        0
    model actually invoked                 anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6   (afeb has landed)
    wall clock                                             25.1 s (sequential, as documented)

**2. THE ACTUAL CACHE FLOOR FOR THE `standard` CLASS IS 1024, NOT 4096.** Direct probe against the
real API: a system block with `cache_control: ephemeral`, called twice, at increasing sizes.

    system tokens   call 1 (write / read)   call 2 (write / read)
      622               0 / 0                  0 / 0
      922               0 / 0                  0 / 0
     1042            1035 / 0                  0 / 1035     <- writes and reads
     1117            1110 / 0                  0 / 1110
     4222            4215 / 0                  0 / 4215

So the repo's `CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS = 4096` (`llm/capabilities.py:330`, documented as the "Opus
4.8 floor") does NOT describe the model `overlap-judge` runs on post-`afeb`. The applicable floor is
**1024**. This resolves the crux this ticket named, in the favourable direction — 4096 would have
made the design dead on arrival.

**3. THE PROPOSED PREFIX IS MARGINAL AGAINST THAT FLOOR, AND THAT IS THE HONEST RISK.** `system +
FIRST` = 377 + 308 ~= 685 tokens of *text*. But the billed prefix ahead of the cache breakpoint also
carries the structured-output tool surface: measured per-call input is 1,324 while system +
instructions is only 985, so ~339 tokens of tool/scaffold sit in front. Prefix after the move is
therefore ~1,024 +/- the digest's own size — straddling the floor rather than clearly over it. The
earlier estimate of ~800 tokens per digest was arithmetic; measured digests are 241-362 tokens, so
the prefix is smaller than that estimate predicted.

CONSEQUENCE, stated up front rather than discovered later: the move is **never worse** (identical
bytes, just relocated from the user block to the cacheable system block) but its saving is
CONDITIONAL on the prefix clearing 1024 for the ticket being reviewed. The implementation therefore
ships the relocation and the ticket records the measured after-numbers honestly, including a zero if
that is what the corpus produces.

**NOT PARALLELIZING.** The loop is sequential (`judge.py`, a plain `for cand in candidates:`), so the
first call writes the prefix and the rest read it — the warm-before-fan-out requirement recorded on
this ticket binds only if the loop is parallelized, and this change does not parallelize it. Left
alone deliberately: fanning out cold calls that share a prefix would turn 1 write + N-1 reads into N
premium writes, which is the regression that requirement exists to prevent.

**NO CHILDREN.** The chosen option is a single relocation inside one function in one file plus its
tests. Decomposing it would create children smaller than the 100-LOC floor with no independent
review value.

═══ RESULT: the hoist is implemented and precision is preserved 12/12, but the measured token
outcome is a REGRESSION of +936 (+5.8%), because the hoisted prefix lands at 846 tokens against a
measured 1024 floor. Reported as a regression, not dressed up. ═══

**BEFORE / AFTER, real `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6` calls, same query ticket, same six candidate
digests, same order, 12 calls each.** BEFORE is the shipped `judge.py` reverted via `git stash`, so
the two runs differ only in this change.

                                        BEFORE     AFTER
    stable system prefix (count_tokens)     423       846      floor 1024
    distinct system prompts per batch         1         1
    input_tokens (total)                 16,040    16,976      +936  (+5.8%)
    cache_read_tokens                         0         0
    cache_write_tokens                        0         0
    surfaced findings                        []        []

`cache_write_tokens` did not rise above one prefix write — it stayed at zero, so the "N writes
instead of 1" failure mode did not occur. Nothing cached at all: 846 < 1024. The +936 is the
orientation paragraph that reconciles the base prompt's "you are given TWO digests" framing with
the split, carried on all 12 calls.

**THE FLOOR IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED — and it is 1024, not the 4096 in `capabilities.py:330`.**
Through the real judge request path: an 875-token system prefix gave write 0 / read 0; a
1250-token one gave write 1243 then read 1243 on the next call. Against the bare API the same
boundary appears between 922 (nothing) and 1042 (write 1035, then read 1035). So the caching
machinery works on this exact path and the prefix is simply too small. `count_tokens` over the base
prompt (423) plus each of seven real digests (306-453) gives 728-875 — short of 1024 by 149-296
tokens for every ticket measured.

**PRECISION PRESERVED: relations identical on 12 of 12 ordered pairs.**

    049e#q_first    unrelated        -> unrelated          conf 0.92 -> 0.95
    049e#q_second   unrelated        -> unrelated          conf 0.95 -> 0.95
    061c#q_first    related_distinct -> related_distinct   conf 0.62 -> 0.62
    061c#q_second   related_distinct -> related_distinct   conf 0.35 -> 0.62
    06e0#q_first    unrelated        -> unrelated          conf 0.85 -> 0.85
    06e0#q_second   unrelated        -> unrelated          conf 0.85 -> 0.85
    79d5#q_first    unrelated        -> unrelated          conf 0.92 -> 0.92
    79d5#q_second   unrelated        -> unrelated          conf 0.95 -> 0.85
    cc77#q_first    unrelated        -> unrelated          conf 0.92 -> 0.85
    cc77#q_second   unrelated        -> unrelated          conf 0.92 -> 0.85
    dbf9#q_first    unrelated        -> unrelated          conf 0.95 -> 0.95
    dbf9#q_second   unrelated        -> unrelated          conf 0.95 -> 0.85

No relation changed and no finding changed. Confidences move within sampling variance (the largest
move, 0.35 -> 0.62 on 061c#q_second, is on a `related_distinct` verdict that is not surfaceable
either way, and its `shared_artifact` went from `prompts.resolve_prompt_cached` to the broader
`prompt caching`). The pointer-for-inline-digest substitution did not degrade the judge on this
corpus.

**MUTATION EVIDENCE, BOTH DIRECTIONS.** Restored code: 20 passed, exit 0. Each mutation applied
alone, then reverted:

    M1  judge() stops passing shared_side          -> FAILS test_shared_query_digest_lives_only_in_the_system_prompt,
                                                              test_hoisted_reference_keeps_the_ordered_pair_slots
    M2  system prompt no longer carries the digest -> FAILS test_shared_query_digest_lives_only_in_the_system_prompt
    M3  ordering-2 slot wrong (ref in FIRST twice) -> FAILS both hoist tests
    M4  default path also hoists                   -> FAILS test_judge_one_default_shape_is_unchanged (+ the hoist test)
    M5  missing-corpus candidate judged anyway     -> FAILS test_missing_corpus_digest_makes_no_call

Every new test dies on at least one mutation and passes on the restored tree; no mutation survived.

**GATES, by exit code:** `make lint` 0, `make typecheck` 0,
`pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 6 --dist worksteal` 0 (8968 passed, 39 skipped).

**FOLLOW-UP FILED:** `c403-cc3a-2c6d-4b9d` (ore-wretched-nene), linked `discovered_from` this
ticket — batch candidates per call to close the 149-296 token gap, carrying these numbers and the
precision-parity requirement.

**NOT CHANGED, deliberately:** `capabilities.py`'s `CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS = 4096` is correct for
the Opus-class model it documents; making it model-aware is separate work. One consequence worth
recording: because that constant also gates `warn_if_cache_ineffective`, a silent caching failure at
this sub-4096 call site would never warn.

compiled_state.description:
# Cut the overlap step's token cost: hoist the shared query digest into the cacheable system prefix

## Context / Problem

`rebar review-plan` spends the majority of its input tokens in the Stage-2 overlap judge. Measured
on this repo against the real API after bug `afeb` landed (so `overlap-judge` already runs on the
`standard` class, `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`): 12 judge calls over a 6-candidate corpus of real
`rebar.llm.enrich` digests billed **16,040 input tokens**, with `cache_read_tokens: 0` and
`cache_write_tokens: 0` on every call. A recording proxy runner wrapped around the real runner in
`overlap.judge.judge()` showed the query ticket's digest block present verbatim in the user message
of **12 of 12** calls, while the system prompt was byte-identical across all 12. The bytes that are
identical on every call are paid at full price every time, because they sit in the volatile user
block, which is never a cache prefix.

## Approach

Hoist the one digest that is invariant across a batch — the query ticket's — out of the per-call
user message and into the system prompt, so the shared bytes sit inside the block that already
carries a cache breakpoint. The engine already applies `anthropic_cache_instructions=True` to the
system block at the shared runner seam (`llm/capabilities.py:cache_settings_for`, dispatched from
`llm/structured_run.py`), so no new caching machinery is added; the only reason today's calls cache
nothing is that the stable block is too small. Concretely: `judge_one` gains one keyword-only
argument naming which side of the pair is the hoisted digest, a module-private helper appends the
digest to the system prompt, and another substitutes a fixed reference string into the slot the
hoisted digest vacated.

Exact wording, so nothing load-bearing is left to the implementer's discretion. The system prompt
becomes the base prompt followed by exactly:

    QUERY TICKET DIGEST — one of the two digests named below is given HERE rather than in the
    user message, because it is the same ticket in every pair of this batch. The user message
    names whether it is FIRST or SECOND for the pair at hand; read it in that position.

    <the four-line digest block produced by _digest_block>

and the reference substituted into the vacated slot is exactly
`the QUERY TICKET DIGEST given in your system prompt`. That orientation paragraph also reconciles
the base prompt's framing (`reviewers/overlap_judge.md`: "You are given TWO ticket digests in a
fixed order"), which otherwise implies both digests arrive inline in the user message. It is
appended by `judge.py` rather than edited into `overlap_judge.md`, so the prompt file keeps working
unchanged for the default (non-hoisted) call shape.

`judge()` judges each candidate in BOTH orderings — `(query, cand)` and `(cand, query)` — so the
query digest is FIRST in one and SECOND in the other; passing `"first"` and `"second"` respectively
preserves the directional reading the prompt depends on. Because the hoisted content is the same
query digest either way, the system block is byte-identical across all 2N calls of a batch: one
cache write on the first call, reads on the remaining 2N-1, whenever the prefix is large enough to
cache at all.

**This is NOT a byte-for-byte relocation, and it is NOT assumed to be behaviour-preserving.** The
user block genuinely changes for the query side: an inline digest is replaced by a pointer to
another block, which is a semantic change to a prompt whose own instructions say "false flags are
costly". The engine's `resolve_prompt_cached` precedent (`llm/prompting/prompts.py:438`) is a pure
stable/volatile split that does not change what the model reads, so it underwrites the SHAPE of the
change but not its harmlessness. Behavioural equivalence is therefore a thing this ticket MEASURES,
not a thing it asserts: a verdict-parity run over the same corpus (below) compares the per-pair
`relation`, `shared_artifact` and `confidence` produced by the inline-digest baseline against the
hoisted build, and a divergence is a finding to report, not a rounding error to absorb.

**Riskiest assumption, tested first — and it has already been measured, in the unfavourable
direction.** The design pays off only if the hoisted prefix reaches the model's minimum cacheable
prefix. `llm/capabilities.py:330` hardcodes `CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS = 4096` and documents it as the
*Opus 4.8* floor. Two probes settled what actually applies to `claude-sonnet-4-6`:

| probe | system tokens (Anthropic `count_tokens`) | call 1 write/read | call 2 write/read |
|---|---|---|---|
| bare API, `cache_control` on system | 922 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| bare API | 1042 | 1035 / 0 | 0 / 1035 |
| through the real judge request path | 875 | 0 / 0 | 0 / 0 |
| through the real judge request path | 1250 | 1243 / 0 | 0 / 1243 |

So the real floor is **1024**, not 4096, and the caching machinery demonstrably works on this exact
request path. But the hoisted prefix does not reach it: `count_tokens` over the base prompt plus each
of the seven real digests gives **728–875 tokens** (base 423; digests 306–453) — every one short of
1024 by 149–296 tokens. A scratch run of the hoisted payload against the real API over the same
12 calls confirmed the consequence directly: `cache_read_tokens: 0`, `cache_write_tokens: 0`, and
**16,748** input tokens versus the baseline's 16,040 — a **+708 token (+4.4%) increase**, entirely
attributable to the added orientation paragraph.

**Why land it anyway, stated plainly rather than dressed up as a win.** The hoist is the structural
precondition for any caching of this call site: while the shared digest sits in the user block, no
floor, model change, or prompt growth can ever make it cacheable, and the cost question stays
unanswerable. With the digest in the stable block the entire question collapses to one measurable
number — stable-prefix tokens versus the model's floor — which this ticket pins at 728–875 vs 1024
and hands to the epic as a decided fact instead of an estimate. The residual cost is bounded and
small (one orientation paragraph, ~50 tokens per call), and the criteria below require it to be
reported honestly as a regression if that is what the final measurement shows. The alternative
lever for closing the 149–296 token gap (batching several candidates into one call, which cuts call
count AND raises the prefix past the floor) is deliberately NOT taken here — it changes the judge's
precision contract and belongs on its own ticket, filed as discovered work with these measurements
attached.

Deliberately NOT done here: the loop is not parallelized. `judge()` is a sequential
`for cand in candidates:`, so the first call warms the prefix and the rest read it. Fanning out cold
calls that share a prefix would turn one cache write plus N-1 cheap reads into N premium writes —
strictly worse than today — so parallelism stays out until it can be sequenced behind a completed
warm-up call.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/overlap/judge.py` — the only production change: the keyword-only shared-side
  argument on `judge_one`, the two module-private helpers, and the two call sites in `judge()`.
  Omitting the argument reproduces today's exact request bytes.
- `tests/unit/test_overlap_judge.py` — the new tests below, added to the existing file.

No other file changes. `src/rebar/llm/overlap/retrieve.py` and `src/rebar/llm/overlap/wire.py` were
declared while the BM25F-tightening and fail-safe options were still open; the chosen design touches
neither, and both fail-safes (`wire.overlap_findings`'s `except` and `judge_one`'s `except`) are
preserved unedited. `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/overlap_judge.md` is deliberately NOT edited, for the
reason given above. `llm/capabilities.py`'s 4096 constant is NOT changed here: it is correct for the
Opus-class model it documents, and making it model-aware is separate work filed as discovered.

## Testing

Offline tests drive the real `judge()` through a recording fake runner that captures each
`RunRequest`, so they assert on the ACTUAL request payload, never on a proxy that would pass either
way. The behavioural and token questions are settled by real-API runs recorded on the ticket.

- **Happy path — the shared digest is hoisted and not duplicated.** One query digest, two candidate
  digests (4 calls). Assert every captured `system_prompt` is byte-identical; the query digest block
  appears in it; the query digest block appears in ZERO of the 4 `instructions`; each candidate's
  block appears in its own `instructions`.
- **Ordered-pair semantics survive the hoist.** For the same run, assert the reference string
  occupies the FIRST slot and the candidate block the SECOND slot in ordering 1, and the reverse in
  ordering 2.
- **Failure/edge path.** A runner raising on every call still yields `judge(...) == []` with nothing
  propagating; a candidate absent from the corpus is skipped with no call made.
- **Back-compat edge.** `judge_one` without the new argument produces `system_prompt` and
  `instructions` byte-identical to today's shape.
- **Behavioural equivalence, real API.** The same query ticket and the same candidate corpus are run
  twice — once on the inline-digest baseline, once on the hoisted build — and the per-pair
  `relation`, `shared_artifact` and `confidence` are compared pair by pair.
- **Mutation check, both directions, for every new test:** revert `judge.py`, confirm each new test
  FAILS; restore, confirm it passes. Recorded on the ticket.
- Gates: `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and `pytest -m "not integration and not external" -n 6
  --dist worksteal -q`, judged by exit code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The query digest is sent in the system prompt and nowhere else: a recording-runner test over
      `judge()` shows it in a byte-identical `system_prompt` on every call and in ZERO
      `instructions`; checked by the new test in `tests/unit/test_overlap_judge.py`.
- [ ] Ordered-pair semantics are preserved in the payload: a test asserts the reference string is in
      the FIRST slot for ordering 1 and the SECOND slot for ordering 2, candidate block in the
      other; checked by the new ordering test.
- [ ] Judgement precision is shown, not assumed: a real-API verdict-parity run over one query ticket
      and at least six candidate digests reports, per ordered pair, the baseline vs hoisted
      `relation` / `shared_artifact` / `confidence`, and is recorded as a ticket comment. Any pair
      whose `relation` differs is called out explicitly with its digests; identical relations on
      every pair is the pass condition, and a divergence must be reported rather than averaged away.
- [ ] The step stays advisory and fail-safe: with a runner that raises on every call, `judge()`
      returns `[]` and raises nothing; checked by the extended error test.
- [ ] The default path is byte-identical: `judge_one` without the new keyword argument produces the
      same `system_prompt` and `instructions` as before; checked by the back-compat test.
- [ ] A BEFORE/AFTER measurement from real `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6` calls over the SAME query
      ticket and SAME corpus is recorded as a ticket comment reporting total `input_tokens`,
      `cache_read_tokens` AND `cache_write_tokens` for both runs, plus the `count_tokens` size of the
      hoisted prefix beside the measured 1024 floor. `cache_write_tokens` above one prefix write
      FAILS this criterion. A net token INCREASE is a valid outcome and must be recorded as a
      regression in plain terms, not presented as a win.
- [ ] The measured shortfall is handed on rather than dropped: a follow-up ticket is created and
      linked `discovered_from` this one, carrying the 728–875 vs 1024 numbers and naming the
      call-batching lever as the way to close the gap; checked by the linked ticket id being
      recorded in a comment here.
- [ ] Every new test is mutation-checked in both directions (fails with `judge.py` reverted, passes
      restored) and the evidence recorded as a ticket comment.
- [ ] `make lint`, `make typecheck`, and the non-integration pytest run all exit 0.

file_impact.reason: hoist the shared query digest out of the per-call user message into the cacheable system prefix; judge_one gains the shared-side argument and judge() passes it for both orderings

recording-runner tests asserting the request payload shape: byte-identical system prompt carrying the query digest, zero occurrences in instructions, ordered-pair slots preserved, fail-safe and default path unchanged
